record.original_question: Given a compact complex hypersurface X in P^n with degree at least n + 2 and only normal crossing singularities. Show that the infinitesimal Kobayashi pseudometric on P^n \ X is degenerate at most on a complex hypersurface.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5.4 Given a compact complex hypersurface X in Pn with degree at least n + 2 and only normal crossing singularities. Show that the infinitesimal Kobayashi pseudometric on Pn \ X is degenerate at most on a complex hypersurface. -N. Sibony, sibony@anh.matups.fr

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n(\mathbb{C})$ be a compact complex hypersurface of degree $d \geq n+2$ having only normal crossing singularities (i.e., locally analytically $X$ is given by the vanishing of a product of distinct coordinate functions). Consider the complement $U = \mathbb{P}^n \setminus X$, and let $K_U : TU \to [0,\infty)$ denote its infinitesimal Kobayashi pseudometric, defined for $(p,v) \in TU$ by
$$K_U(p,v) = \inf\{|\xi| : \exists\, f : \mathbb{D} \to U \text{ holomorphic with } f(0)=p,\ df_0(\xi)=v\},$$
where $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$ is the unit disc. The degeneracy locus of $K_U$ is the set of $p \in U$ such that there exists $0 \neq v \in T_p U$ with $K_U(p,v) = 0$. Prove that this degeneracy locus is contained in a complex hypersurface of $U$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this problem. It was posed by N. Sibony as a problem on hyperbolicity of complements of hypersurfaces of degree at least n+2 in projective space, a context closely tied to the still-open Kobayashi conjecture on hyperbolicity of generic high-degree hypersurface complements. No source confirming a complete solution was located.

status_evidence.title: On some problems of Kobayashi and Lang; algebraic approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Kobayashi/Lang hyperbolicity problems for hypersurface complements in projective space; degeneracy of the Kobayashi pseudometric on complements of high-degree hypersurfaces remains a central open question.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity-type questions for complements of hypersurfaces of degree at least n+2 in P^n remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Kobayashi metric - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Kobayashi conjecture predicts that a general hypersurface of large degree d in P^{n+1} is Kobayashi hyperbolic, and that the complement of such a hypersurface (of suitable degree) in P^n is hyperbolic.
status_evidence.claim: The associated Kobayashi conjecture for complements is still considered open in full generality.
